Although I did enjoy the time I spent playing this game, and the expansion content wherein, I feel that Donuts for Deer Teeth falls a bit short of a full experience. Although there were no egregious bugs, I feel the levels are very rough around the edges, and the game systems are not fully developed. Although this is a linear level based game, there are rouge-like elements pasted in in terms of items and abilities. and I'm not sure it really fits. And to get to my main point, despite the central theme of the game being expansion, besides seeing your boobs grow to ridiculous size (of which I am a fan) there is little game-play incentive to keep expanding your character beyond the point where they get the crush ability. Eating donuts will make the sprite for your boobs get bigger, however the sprite never changes to reflect straining against fabric, and doesn't seem to have collision. Sadly, no matter how gargantuan you get from then on out it has no effect on your character's damage, speed, defense, or ability to enter narrow doorways. Although you can feed your donuts to the Cryptid and watch her swell up like a balloon, feeding her more than 1 donut a day doesn't seem to grant any game play advantages. I'm not a huge fan of belly/fat inflation, so maybe this game isn't wholly for me. Game-play is little more than run around and knock out "cops" with a baseball bat and collect donuts. Other than that, in between levels you can talk to a whole bunch of generously proportioned fursonas each day (I think those must have been supporters), and collect photographs (which do not save between playthroughs). If there was a Although I don't really feel like giving it a thumbs down, I do want people to know this game is a little light on content. In the end, although I enjoyed this game I'm not sure this is quite worth 7 dollars. Maybe get it if it's on sale.

This game does a lot of things that I really like. Addressing the elephant in the room it’s obviously a game meant to titillate the viewer and I enjoy it on that front; the graphical style and what the style is used to render upon the screen is delightful, no notes. However, the mechanics are also fun; at the end of each round you choose which upgrades and equipment you’d like to take with you and by the end of a run your character is going to be a little bit different each time. It feels like there’s a nice balance of items that favour the stealth and combat aspects of the game. Something that I appreciate is that even though runs have a stochastic character due to the varied offerings presented during gameplay the maps are not; I found this particularly helpful as it took me an embarrassing number of attempts before I realized that the levels I’d been playing through had an entirely hidden area equal to (if not larger) than the area of the level I had been aware of. The sound cues for the enemies were of particular significance in the areas where the lighting was lacking, but from start to finish the sound design for combat was instrumental in communicating the impact of damage that was being dealt and the speed at which the combatants were moving. The main element of the game that I relished was the story. The tale we traverse is straightforward, communicates our character’s motivations, and establishes the relationships between various characters and groups. It’s short and simple, mostly being drip fed by your new friend and a handful of the friendly NPC’s you encounter within the hub area as the game goes on. That being said, the dominating reason behind my enjoyment of the story in question is because it flatters my pre-existing political sentiments and presents a caricature of a world that I find structurally isomorphic to the one we inhabit.

Honestly, this game is an absolute blast and well worth playing. It might lean on the shorter side, but it doesn't waste any time. Every single day scales up the difficulty and throws tougher challenges at you, which is exactly how a solid arcade-style gameplay loop should handle progression. The core mechanics are actually pretty unique for a fast-paced, top-down brawler. You're basically running around brawling guards, using things like baseball bats or different unique weapons across the levels, and stealing sweets. But the real strategy comes down to a choice-driven growth mechanic where you have to balance two options: * Feed Mari (the deer spirit in the woods): Doing this unlocks new items and lets you choose between rewards she offers. The more you feed her, the larger she gets, and you can progressively see her growth animations with each stage. This is where the fetish/kink content comes into play, and the animations are really well done. * Eat the donuts yourself: If you choose to keep the food, your own breasts grow larger. This unlocks a dedicated feature/attack mechanic and lets you continuously upgrade its capabilities to take down guards. Beyond the main loop, there are also hidden collectibles like pinup art scattered around the maps, and a bunch of achievements to hunt for. Some of the achievements are genuinely tough and will test your skills, but they give you a great excuse to thoroughly explore every level and try out different weapon styles. At the end of the day, it's just a really fun, rewarding game that actually has solid mechanical depth. It stands out completely from the usual generic titles on Steam. If you don't mind the adult theme, the gameplay itself holds up great.
